system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Containers often contain AGENTS.md files. These files can appear anywhere in the container's filesystem.
system_prompt_style.note: System message shown is fixed text, but AGENTS.md files and deferred discovery of skills/MCP tools add runtime-loaded content; mechanism of assembly not shown in code. Paper-only evidence.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Codex can read and edit files, as well as run commands including test harnesses, linters, and type checkers.
env_context_strategy.note: AGENTS.md guidance may also inform navigation; no injected file tree described.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Tool output is capped at 10,000 tokens by default unless the model requests a different limit.
context_compaction.evidence_locator: How GPT-5.6 fuses frontier intelligence with frontier efficiency, Avoid context bloat
context_compaction.note: 'summarize' inferred from mention of 'better auto-compaction in Codex core' (App Server post); mechanism not described.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Codex provides verifiable evidence of its actions through citations of terminal logs and test outputs
observation_format.note: Launch post states image inputs lacking at launch; later versions not documented in evidence.

tool_call_format.note: No parser or tool-call syntax described; only blog posts available.

edit_primitive.note: Edit tool definition not in evidence; posts only say it can edit files and emit diffs.

tool_schema_source.note: Schema source for built-in tools not described; MCP servers are wired in per App Server post, but full list unknown.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Run codex mcp-server⁠(opens in a new window) and connect from any MCP client that supports stdio servers
protocol_standardization.evidence_locator: Unlocking the Codex harness, Choosing the right protocol
protocol_standardization.note: Also MCP client ('wires up integrations like MCP servers'); 'other' = Codex App Server JSON-RPC protocol (proprietary-published, JSON-RPC lite).

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: listen to Codex core’s internal event stream, and then transform those low-level events into a small set of stable, UI-ready JSON-RPC notifications.
loop_primitives.evidence_locator: Unlocking the Codex harness, Inside the Codex harness
loop_primitives.note: React loop inferred from 'One user turn can contain many model and tool iterations' (GPT-5.6 post).

planning_granularity.note: No plan object or planning mechanism described in evidence.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Codex core is both a library where all the agent code lives and a runtime that can be spun up to run the agent loop and manage the persistence of one Codex thread
multi_agent_topology.evidence_locator: Unlocking the Codex harness, Inside the Codex harness
multi_agent_topology.note: Desktop app orchestrates many agents in parallel as independent threads; no delegation topology described.

delegation_mechanism.note: No delegation mechanism described; no tool registry available.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: the server may ask for client approval before it can run an action by sending a server request. The approval will pause the turn until the client replies with either “allow” or “deny.”
human_in_loop.evidence_locator: Unlocking the Codex harness, The conversation primitives
human_in_loop.note: 'configurable' from 'runtime settings, such as approval policies' (GPT-5.6 post). Default policy not stated.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: A thread is the durable container for an ongoing Codex session between a user and an agent. It contains multiple turns.
short_term_state.evidence_locator: Unlocking the Codex harness, The conversation primitives

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Codex can be guided by AGENTS.md files placed within your repository.
long_term_memory.note: AGENTS.md are human-written instruction files rather than agent-written memory; skills mentioned in App Server post ('wires up integrations like MCP servers and skills').

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Codex creates, resumes, forks, and archives threads, and persists the event history so clients can reconnect and render a consistent timeline.
state_persistence.evidence_locator: Unlocking the Codex harness, Inside the Codex harness

self_verification.note: Tests/linters are run by the model per prompt instruction ('you MUST run all of them'), not harness-enforced; no harness verifier described.

retry_policy.note: No task-level retry mechanism described; no run loop available.

rollback.note: Threads can be forked; no revert/undo mechanism described. Prompt instructs git commits but no harness rollback shown.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: ends when the agent finishes producing outputs for that input
termination_condition.evidence_locator: Unlocking the Codex harness, The conversation primitives
termination_condition.note: Other caps not described; run loop not in evidence.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: the harness treats all model-visible history as append-only: new messages, tool results, and environment updates are added at the end rather than inserted into earlier context.
cost_controls.evidence_locator: How GPT-5.6 fuses frontier intelligence with frontier efficiency, Preserve exact prefixes for prompt caching
cost_controls.note: Budget caps and routing not described.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: The Codex agent operates entirely within a secure, isolated container in the cloud.
execution_isolation.note: Cloud Codex/Web; CLI and desktop run locally with a sandbox ('Codex executes shell/file tools in a sandbox') of unspecified kind. Coded cloud product as described.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: These files can appear anywhere in the container's filesystem.

network_policy.evidence_quote: During task execution, internet access is disabled
network_policy.note: Launch configuration; June 2025 update lets users enable internet access (configurable).

permission_model.note: Approval requests and 'consistent policy model' exist but default authorisation policy not stated.

tracing.evidence_quote: Items are typed (e.g., user message, agent message, tool execution, approval request, diff) and each has an explicit lifecycle
tracing.evidence_locator: Unlocking the Codex harness, The conversation primitives

replayability.note: Resume/fork described but no replay facility discussed; no code available.

guardrails.note: Model trained to refuse malware requests (not harness guardrail); approvals exist; no filter/policy config shown.
